title: Python attribute-write heavy read-side shapes: subclass-to-base, cross-module __class__, diamond super (DEC-303 a80 GCLI-151c)
description: Record-only held task, the heavy read-side half (leader label GCLI-151c) of GCLI-151 split under DEC-303 (a80) item 6 (opum-ai/opum-doc#2083, ODOC-640). Shapes: (6) Q-C a subclass write self.m = other leaves a base self.m() resolving, because the MRO guard walks the receiver MRO, not its descendants; (17) N7 an __init__ that writes self.__class__ = Other leaves outside receivers x = C(); x.m() resolving across a module boundary; (18) N8 diamond super, where D(B, C) gives the edge A.m although a D instance super() after B reaches C.m. Each is at or above the not-small line: #6 and #17 are cross-module or descendant propagation, and #18 changes super() from the defining class static MRO to the call-site receiver runtime MRO, a core resolution-model change. Do NOT build any of these until the leader relays an opum-doc ruling or a bounded measurement ruling for it; the leader is routing #18, #6 and #17 to opum-doc as a scoping question. Dev results measured 2026-11-27 at origin/dev 1ea3432: wrong edges B.m, m.py:C.m and A.m respectively.
